---
title: Upload and download files
sidebar_label: Upload and download files
description: Upload a file's bytes, make the item that names them, download them, hand out a link that expires, and replace them.
job: A builder uploads bytes, makes the item that names them, downloads them, hands out an expiring link and replaces them.
---

A file is two parts: a blob, the bytes, and a file item that names the blob by its hash and carries the title and everything else. Upload the bytes, then create the item. [Files](/build/files) explains why the two are apart.

To upload, your key needs write on a type outside `system.*`, or `blobs.manage`, and to create the item, write on its type. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. In the Swift examples, `copy` is an [open working copy](/reference/swift-sdk/working-copy#open-a-copy).

## Upload the bytes

[Upload a blob](/reference/api/blobs/uploadBlob) takes the bytes as the request body, **as they are rather than as a form**, with their media type as the `Content-Type`. Marfa answers the blob's `hash`, `mime_type` and `size_bytes`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /blobs
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: text/plain

<the bytes of reading-list.txt>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: blob, error } = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: await readFile("reading-list.txt"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain" },
});
if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let upload = try await copy.blobs.put(file: fileURL, mimeType: "text/plain")
guard let hash = upload.blob else { return }
```

The same bytes always give the same hash, so uploading them again **stores nothing more**. An upload has no size cap: Marfa ends one only when no bytes arrive for 60 seconds.

## Point an item at the bytes

Create a file item whose **`blob_ref`** is the hash. `core.file` takes any file, and `core.file.image`, `core.file.audio`, `core.file.video` and `core.file.webpage` fit their kinds.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.file --prop title=reading-list.txt \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 \
  --prop mime_type=text/plain
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "reading-list.txt",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: created } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.file",
    properties: { title: "reading-list.txt", blob_ref: blob.hash, mime_type: blob.mime_type },
  },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
_ = try await copy.items.create(Draft(
    type: "core.file",
    properties: ["title": "reading-list.txt", "blob_ref": .string(hash), "mime_type": "text/plain"]))
```

`marfa items add reading-list.txt` uploads and creates in one command. A housekeeping job then reads the bytes and adds what the item lacks, such as `extracted_text`, so [a search](/build/list-filter-search#search) finds the file by its words.

**Until an item names the hash, the bytes can't be read**, even with the key that uploaded them. A file item may name only bytes its writer uploaded or can already read, so upload with **the same key** that writes the item: any other hash is refused `404 blob_not_found`.

## Attach a file to a note or another item

To attach a file to a note or any other item, link them with an `attached-to` edge from the file item, as `marfa items attach <id> photo.jpg` does in one command. The file is then an **attachment**: it goes to the bin with the last item it's attached to, and comes back with any of them ([Edges](/build/edges)). A synced folder does it from the note's [`has-attachment` line](/use/work-with-folder-files#attach-a-file-to-a-note).

## Download the bytes

[Download a blob](/reference/api/blobs/downloadBlob) answers the bytes as they were uploaded. Marfa sends them as an attachment named after the hash, so take the file's name from the item's **`title`**. A `Range` header such as `bytes=0-1023` gets part of a blob.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs download sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --output reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: bytes } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash } },
  parseAs: "arrayBuffer",
});
await writeFile("reading-list.txt", Buffer.from(bytes!));
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let bytes = try await copy.blobs.withFile(hash) { url in try Data(contentsOf: url) }
```

A blob you may not read answers `404 blob_not_found`, like a missing one, and `503 blob_store_unavailable` means try again later. In Swift, read the file inside the closure, because the copy can remove it afterward ([Keep files in a working copy](/build/keep-files-in-a-working-copy)).

## Hand out a time-limited link

An image element in a web page can't send your key. [Get a blob URL](/reference/api/blobs/getBlobUrl) answers a link that serves the bytes to anyone who has it. `ttl_seconds` is **an hour by default, and at most seven days**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs url sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --ttl-seconds 900
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0/url?ttl_seconds=900
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: link } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}/url", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash }, query: { ttl_seconds: 900 } },
});
```

Marfa checks your read **when it makes the link**, so revoking your key doesn't end a link early. Ask for a link when you need one, with the shortest lifetime that serves, and **don't store it**.

## Replace a file's bytes

Upload the replacement, then update the file item's `blob_ref` to its hash, **naming the version you read**, as [Update items without losing changes](/build/write-safely) shows:

```bash
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
marfa items update <id> --version 2 \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:7623dfe0bbb9b127e9d68350ac7d9168fecfb3ac404778057b116315d3205780
```

Marfa clears what it read from the old bytes, such as `extracted_text`, unless the same write names it, and reads the new bytes. The old blob stays **as long as an earlier version** of the item names it.

The rules are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md) chapter of the contract.
